question:
A random variable $X$ has the probability distribution
$X: 0,1,2,3$
$P(X): k,2k,3k,4k$.
(i) Find the value of $k$.
(ii) Hence find $P(X\leq1)$ and $P(X>1)$.
explanation:
Step 1: Probability-distribution condition
The sum of the probabilities corresponding to all possible values of a random variable must be $1$. Therefore, $$k+2k+3k+4k=1.$$
Step 2: Determination of the parameter
$$10k=1\quad\Rightarrow\quad k=\frac1{10}.$$
Step 3: Calculation of $P(X\leq1)$
The values satisfying $X\leq1$ are $0$ and $1$. Hence, $$P(X\leq1)=P(X=0)+P(X=1)=k+2k=3k=\frac3{10}.$$
Step 4: Calculation of $P(X>1)$
The relevant values are $2$ and $3$. Thus, $$P(X>1)=3k+4k=7k=\frac7{10}.$$
Step 5: Verification and conclusion
Since $\frac3{10}+\frac7{10}=1$, the two complementary results are consistent. Therefore, $$\boxed{k=\frac1{10},\quad P(X\leq1)=\frac3{10},\quad P(X>1)=\frac7{10}}.$$
